title: Window Functions
learning_outcomes: Describe the main purpose and behavior of window functions.

content.intro: This lesson covers window functions as part of SQLite’s embedded relational database model. Work through one small example, verify the output, and then connect the result to the listed subtopics from the supplied curriculum.
content.why_it_matters: Window functions preserve individual rows while calculating across related rows.
content.task: Create a second example for window functions. Use at least one of these subtopics: Window clauses, PARTITION BY, Window ordering. Predict the result, run it in a local SQLite environment or supported language binding, and document one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Include a minimal reproducible SQL statement or application snippet.
State the expected result before execution and compare it to the observed result.
Document one boundary/error case and the SQLite runtime assumptions.
hints: Start from the smallest subtopic and a fixture with only a few known rows.

items.title: Window clauses
items.text: Window functions calculate across related rows while preserving each output row. Define PARTITION BY, ORDER BY and frame boundaries intentionally; ties may produce different rankings depending on the chosen function.

items.title: Aggregate window calculations
items.text: Aggregate functions summarize groups. WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups. Remember that aggregates generally skip NULL inputs and verify how COUNT(*) differs from COUNT(column).

content_blocks.title: Example: Window Functions
content_blocks.code:
WITH scores(name, points) AS (VALUES ('Ari', 8), ('Bea', 10))
SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY points DESC) FROM scores;
